He played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for the [[New Jersey Nets]], [[Denver Nuggets]], [[Dallas Mavericks]], [[Orlando Magic]], and [[Phoenix Suns]]. His daughter Aniya Harvey appeared on the eighth season of ''[[Love Island (American TV series) season 8|Love Island USA]]''. ==High school career== Harvey was born in [[Shellman, Georgia]]. He attended Randolph-Clay High School in [[Cuthbert, Georgia]] where he was the consensus 1999 national high school player of the year. In 1999, he was in the McDonald's All-America Game, was in the USA Today All-USA 1st Team in 1999, and got the Naismith Award as nation's top high school player in 1999.{{Cite web|url=http://hoopshype.com/players/donnell_harvey.htm|title = NBA Players}} ==College career== Harvey accepted an athletic scholarship to attend the [[University of Florida]] in Gainesville, Florida, where he played for coach [[Billy Donovan]]'s [[Florida Gators men's basketball]] team during the 1999–2000 season. After starting three-fourths of the Gators' first 12 games, he lost his starting spot to Brent Wright after returning home over the New Year's break because of homesickness. Harvey averaged 10.2 points, 7.0 rebounds and 1.0 assists per game {{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2000/04/28/sports/plus-college-basketball-florida-freshman-forward-is-turning-pro.html?src=pm|title=PLUS: COLLEGE BASKETBALL – FLORIDA; Freshman Forward is Turning Pro|newspaper=The New York Times|date=April 28, 2000}} and was voted to the SEC All-Freshman Team in his only season playing college basketball. ==Professional career== Harvey was selected by the [[New York Knicks]] with the 22nd overall pick of the [[2000 NBA draft]] and then traded, along with [[John Wallace (basketball)|John Wallace]], to the Mavericks in exchange for [[Erick Strickland]] and [[Pete Mickeal]]. He was in Dallas until he was traded to the Denver Nuggets in February 2002. Harvey then latched on to the Orlando Magic in September 2003, only to be traded to the Phoenix Suns in December 2003. He was signed then waived by the Atlanta Hawks in October 2004. Harvey joined the Sioux Falls Skyforce of the [[Continental Basketball Association]] (CBA) in December 2004. He was called up to the New Jersey Nets in February 2005 but was waived 2 weeks later after only playing 3 games for team. Harvey's final NBA game ever was played on February 13, 2005, in a 94–79 win over the Denver Nuggets. Harvey played for 2 minutes and the only stat he recorded was 1 rebound. Harvey then played for Panionios (Greece) from September 2005 until March 2006. He then went to [[Beşiktaş J.K. (men's basketball)|Beşiktaş]] (Turkey) in 2006–07, then later went to Rieti (Italy) in July 2007. Harvey has also played for [[Banvitspor]] in [[Turkey]] and the [[Gigantes de Carolina (men's basketball)|Carolina Giants]] in [[Puerto Rico]] (2009).{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/index.aspx|title=Besiktas Emlakjet Istanbul basketball, News, Roster, Rumors, Stats, Awards, Transactions, Details-eurobasket|website=Eurobasket LLC}} In November 2010, Harvey signed with the Bosnian club [[KK Igokea]]. After playing for [[Jiangsu]] in the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] for the 2008–09 and 2009–10 seasons,{{Cite web | title=NiuBBall.com » Donnel Harvey | url=http://www.niubball.com/tag/donnel-harvey/ | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111222034417/http://www.niubball.com:80/tag/donnel-harvey/ | access-date=2026-01-28 | archive-date=2011-12-22}} Harvey played 32 games with [[Tianjin Ronggang]] for the 2011–12 season,{{Cite web|url=http://www.asia-basket.com/team.asp?Cntry=CHN&Team=3512|title = Tianjin Ronggang Pioneers basketball, News, Roster, Rumors, Stats, Awards, Transactions, Details-asia-basket}} averaging 24.7 points and 14.7 rebounds per game.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/world/asia/35949/rodney-white-inks-in-the-philippines-donnell-harvey-to-join-him.html|title=Sportsglory | Product Guides for Athletes & Sports Records}} He joined the [[Talk 'N Text Tropang Texters]] replacing the injured [[Omar Samhan]] for the 2012 [[PBA Commissioner's Cup]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/sports/basketball/250522/pba-harvey-debuts-for-commissioner-s-cup-champions-talk-n-text/story/|title=PBA: Harvey debuts for Commissioner's Cup champions Talk 'N Text|date=March 6, 2012|website=GMA News Online}} He led the Texters to the finals, but the team ultimately lost to the B-Meg Llamados 4–3. During Game 7 of the Finals, he fouled out late in the 4th quarter despite having a superb performance. Later that year, he returned to Tianjin Ronggang.[http://www.niubball.com/teams/ Niubball.com – Teams] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203154411/http://www.niubball.com/teams/ |date=December 3, 2013 }}.
